title: Audit forwarder: loss detection and contract-level reconciliation for SIEM/webhook sinks
creator: Jonah Reyes
description: Problem: External SIEM and webhook sinks (Splunk, Datadog, generic HTTP) occasionally observe gaps or reordering during high-throughput bursts or downstream rate limiting. Existing model relies on best-effort retry + DLQ but lacks an efficient end-to-end loss detection and reconciliation mechanism at the per-tenant contract level. Goal: Add a lightweight reconciliation layer and stronger delivery contracts so we can detect and repair lost audit events, preserve ordering within logical streams where required, and provide actionable observability for customers and SREs. Scope: Implement watermarking and per-sink delivery checkpoints, periodic ledger reconciliation, and a reconciliation API for manual/automated repair. Integrations: Splunk HEC, Datadog HTTP intake, generic webhook fanout. Out of scope: full exactly-once semantics for multi-sink fanout in this cycle (we'll aim for at-least-once + repair).
acceptance_criteria: Per-sink checkpointing exists: each audit-forwarder persists a monotonically increasing delivery offset for each external contract and persists last-ack timestamp.
A reconciliation job can enumerate a tenant's audit ledger and detect holes between last-delivered offsets and source offsets within 5 minutes of occurrence.
Reconciler can push missing events to a repair queue that is rate-limited per-sink and tagged for idempotent delivery, with observable metrics.
Ordering preservation for ordered sinks (customer-configurable) is maintained using per-key ordering buckets and backoff-based retries that avoid reordering beyond a configurable window.

Integration tests covering Splunk HEC and Datadog intake show no gaps under simulated 3x normal burst with injected 429/503 responses and a reconciliation repair that heals gaps within 2 minutes in test harness.
Documentation for admin console: per-contract delivery state, last-checkpoint, repair actions, and SLA implications are published.
Security: reconciliation endpoints require tenant-scoped auth and all repair payloads are logged to immutable audit store before re-delivery.
plan: Design: finalize checkpoint schema (watermark + per-sink vector) and reconciliation contract (2/12 - complete)
Prototype: augment forwarder to persist checkpoints to durable store and emit metrics (2/14 - 2/20)

Integrations: add Splunk HEC idempotency headers and Datadog backoff adapters (2/24 - 3/02)
Tests: fault-injection harness and chaos tests for ordering/429/timeout scenarios (2/27 - 3/05)
Docs + Console: admin controls and repair UI + runbook (3/03 - 3/10)

Postmortem and playbook: capture lessons in runbook and iterate if DLQ volumes > baseline after rollout
